judged_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest));` treats email addresses as case-sensitive, so adding `ALICE@example.com` to a booking already containing `alice@example.com` creates a duplicate attendee and sends duplicate calendar invitations (P2, confidence: 100).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `uniqueGuests` is filtered using direct string comparison `guest === attendee.email` without any case normalization. Email addresses are case-insensitive per RFC 5321, so 'ALICE@example.com' and 'alice@example.com' should be treated as the same address. The code would allow adding 'ALICE@example.com' when 'alice@example.com' already exists, creating duplicate attendees. The blacklist check also uses case-sensitive comparison via `includes()`. This is a real bug that could cause duplicate calendar invitations.
